title: Asymmetric Information and R&D Disclosure: Evidence from Scientific Publications
authors: Stefano Horst Baruffaldi; Markus Simeth; David Wehrheim
eligible_reason: Stacked DiD: 43 brokerage merger/closure events (2001-2011), each forming its own treated/control cohort with a six-year window; firms appear in multiple event stacks (1,384 of 1,504 firms; 107,621 duplicated firm-years) and regressions include event (E_ID) fixed effects with POST and TREATED defined within stack. Stacked designs are excluded by the protocol.
design_notes: bsw2022+data+T2.dta: 122,429 firm-event-year rows, 23,035 firm-event pairs, FYEAR 1997-2014. Table 2: areg Y TREATED_X_POST POST TREATED [controls] i.E_ID i.FYEAR, abs(FIRM_ID) cl(FIRM_ID), outcomes COV, BASPRD, LN_PUB, IHS_PUB. Table 3 same on a propensity-score matched sample with aw=_weight. Table 4 heterogeneity splits (high/low x TREATED_X_POST). Table 5 alternative outcomes with controls. Figure 1 stacked event-study dummies TREATED_d_window1-6. Table 6 is an OLS attention regression. No unstacked firm-level first-treatment variable is provided; an unstacked TWFE would have to be reconstructed from E_ID event dates.
estimators_reported: stacked TWFE DiD (areg with event FE)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 11 distinct event years across 43 events (stacked); not an unstacked staggered design.

ineligible_specs.reason: stacked DiD with event-cohort FE; firms repeated across stacks

screener_notes: Anonymized final analysis datasets (Compustat/CRSP/IBES/Scopus-derived) are included with a single master do-file. The design is Hong-Kacperczyk style stacked brokerage-shock DiD; eligible only if the protocol were relaxed to allow stacked designs. Recorded as not eligible.
